subject: Higher Mathematics
question:
If \( m, n, x > 0 \) and \( m \neq 1, n \neq 1 \), then —
i) \( 2\log \sqrt{m} + 3\log \sqrt{n} = 5 \)
ii) \( \log m + \log n - \log x = \log \frac{mn}{x} \)
iii) \( m^2 = \sqrt[3]{m^2} \), where \( x = \frac{2}{3} \)
Correct: ii only
explanation:
(i) Simplifies to \( \log m + \frac{3}{2} \log n \), not necessarily 5. (ii) True by logarithm rules. (iii) Simplifies to \( m^2 = m^{2/3} \Rightarrow m^{4/3}=1 \Rightarrow m=1 \), but \( m \neq 1 \), so false.

subject: Higher Mathematics
question:
For logarithm—
i) \( \log_2 7 = \frac{\log_{10} 7}{\log_{10} 2} \)
ii) \( \log_6 64 = 4 \)
iii) \( \log_2 \left( \frac{128}{32} \right) = 2 \)
Correct: i and iii
explanation:
(i) True by change of base formula. (ii) False, since \( 6^4 = 1296 \neq 64 \). (iii) True, \( \log_2 (128/32) = \log_2 4 = 2 \).
